set_in_point.note: I: p.400 'By default on United States keyboards, the Mark IN key is the I key'; E: Mark IN icon on E in the 2026 illustration (labelled Mark IN in the 1999 chart).

set_out_point.note: O: 'the Mark OUT key is the O key'; R: Mark OUT icon in the 2026 illustration (labelled in the 1999 chart).

clear_in_point.note: Keyboard Settings illustration ("Keyboard - MC English (United States)", Editing Guide p.1205); key names from Avid's labelled Windows NT keyboard chart, whose icons match the 2026 illustration key for key

clear_out_point.note: Keyboard Settings illustration ("Keyboard - MC English (United States)", Editing Guide p.1205); key names from Avid's labelled Windows NT keyboard chart, whose icons match the 2026 illustration key for key

clear_in_out.note: Keyboard Settings illustration ("Keyboard - MC English (United States)", Editing Guide p.1205); key names from Avid's labelled Windows NT keyboard chart, whose icons match the 2026 illustration key for key

set_range_to_clip.note: Keyboard Settings illustration ("Keyboard - MC English (United States)", Editing Guide p.1205); key names from Avid's labelled Windows NT keyboard chart, whose icons match the 2026 illustration key for key. Marks IN/OUT at the clip under the position indicator on selected tracks.

insert_edit.note: Editing Guide: 'Press the V key to perform a splice-in edit'.

overwrite_edit.note: Editing Guide: 'Press the B key to perform an overwrite edit'.

lift_edit.note: Keyboard Settings illustration ("Keyboard - MC English (United States)", Editing Guide p.1205); key names from Avid's labelled Windows NT keyboard chart, whose icons match the 2026 illustration key for key

extract_edit.note: Keyboard Settings illustration ("Keyboard - MC English (United States)", Editing Guide p.1205); key names from Avid's labelled Windows NT keyboard chart, whose icons match the 2026 illustration key for key

replace_edit.note: Button on the Edit tab of the Command palette; not on the default keyboard.

fit_to_fill_edit.note: Button on the Edit tab of the Command palette (overwrite with a variable-speed effect); not on the default keyboard.

split_at_playhead.note: Guide: 'you must first map the Add Edit button onto the keyboard' (MultiCam chapter).

add_default_transition.note: Keyboard Settings illustration ("Keyboard - MC English (United States)", Editing Guide p.1205); key names from Avid's labelled Windows NT keyboard chart, whose icons match the 2026 illustration key for key. Adds the default dissolve at the nearest transition on selected tracks.

add_audio_crossfade.note: Same command: Add Dissolve on selected audio tracks is the audio crossfade; Avid has no separate audio-only command. Same key as add_default_transition.

lift_clip.note: p.622-623: 'By default, Media Composer deletes the selected segment and leaves blank space' when Delete is pressed with selected segments.

delete_clip.note: Delete closes the gap only when the yellow Extract/Splice-in segment tool is active (or set as Default Segment Tool); there is no separate default key for a ripple delete.

cut_clip.note: p.624 'Cutting, Copying, and Pasting in the Timeline': selected segments.

copy_clip.note: p.624: selected segments. (The C key is 'Copy to Clipboard' of IN-OUT marked material, a different command.)

paste_clip.note: p.624: pastes the segment at the position indicator using the default segment tool.

create_multicam.note: 2009 sheet: 'Shift + Ctrl + G creates a Group Clip'; the 2026.8 ReadMe names Ctrl+Shift+G among the modifier shortcuts 'for Multicam editing'. A group clip is Avid's multicam clip.

move_clips_up_a_track.note: p.~617: 'The Move Clip Up and Move Clip Down keys are assigned to the up and down arrows of the default keyboard settings.' (In MultiCamera editing the same arrows are Previous/Next In Group.)

move_clips_down_a_track.note: Same sentence as Move Clip Up.

nudge_clips_back.note: Keyboard Settings illustration ("Keyboard - MC English (United States)", Editing Guide p.1205); key names from Avid's labelled Windows NT keyboard chart, whose icons match the 2026 illustration key for key. Guide p.621: segments move horizontally 'using the Trim left and Trim right keys'.

nudge_clips_forward.note: Keyboard Settings illustration ("Keyboard - MC English (United States)", Editing Guide p.1205); key names from Avid's labelled Windows NT keyboard chart, whose icons match the 2026 illustration key for key. Same as nudge_clips_back.

nudge_clips_back_many.note: Keyboard Settings illustration ("Keyboard - MC English (United States)", Editing Guide p.1205); key names from Avid's labelled Windows NT keyboard chart, whose icons match the 2026 illustration key for key. 10 frames (8 in 24p).

nudge_clips_forward_many.note: Keyboard Settings illustration ("Keyboard - MC English (United States)", Editing Guide p.1205); key names from Avid's labelled Windows NT keyboard chart, whose icons match the 2026 illustration key for key. 10 frames (8 in 24p).

trim_edit_back.note: Keyboard Settings illustration ("Keyboard - MC English (United States)", Editing Guide p.1205); key names from Avid's labelled Windows NT keyboard chart, whose icons match the 2026 illustration key for key. Same keys as the nudge actions: in Avid one key trims a selected transition or moves selected

trim_edit_forward.note: Keyboard Settings illustration ("Keyboard - MC English (United States)", Editing Guide p.1205); key names from Avid's labelled Windows NT keyboard chart, whose icons match the 2026 illustration key for key

trim_edit_back_many.note: Keyboard Settings illustration ("Keyboard - MC English (United States)", Editing Guide p.1205); key names from Avid's labelled Windows NT keyboard chart, whose icons match the 2026 illustration key for key

trim_edit_forward_many.note: Keyboard Settings illustration ("Keyboard - MC English (United States)", Editing Guide p.1205); key names from Avid's labelled Windows NT keyboard chart, whose icons match the 2026 illustration key for key

trim_tool.note: Keyboard Settings illustration ("Keyboard - MC English (United States)", Editing Guide p.1205); key names from Avid's labelled Windows NT keyboard chart, whose icons match the 2026 illustration key for key. Trim chapter table: 'U Nearest transition'.

select_edit_point.note: Trim chapter p.653 table: U = nearest transition, A = previous, S = next. Side cycling is P / [ / ] (Trim A Side / AB Sides / B Side, editor_only). Same key as trim_tool.

extend_edit.note: Button on the Trim tab of the Command palette ('You can map the Extend button'); Avid extends to the Mark IN/OUT, not the playhead.

trim_in_to_playhead.note: Top button (Edit tab of the Command palette): extracts from the start of the clip to the position indicator.

trim_out_to_playhead.note: Tail button (Edit tab of the Command palette): extracts from the position indicator to the end of the clip.

freeze_frame.note: Menu command Composer > Freeze Frame; no default key given.

add_marker.note: Guide: 'Map the Add Marker button to a key ... Drag an Add Marker button to a key on the Keyboard palette'.

prev_marker.note: 'Click the Go to Previous Marker button in the Move tab of the Command palette'.

next_marker.note: 'Click the Go to Next Marker button in the Move tab of the Command palette'.

match_frame_program_to_source.note: Match Frame button 'appears by default in the second row of buttons below the Source monitor'; not on the default keyboard.

match_frame_source_to_program.note: 'Click the Reverse Match Frame button in the Other tab of the Command palette'.

play_around_edit.note: 'The Play Loop button does not appear in Source/Record mode by default. You must map it'. Its Trim-mode key is not given in text (see unverifiable).

key_linear.note: Right-click menu on the keyframe graph/track; no default key.

leave_compound.note: Timeline bottom-toolbar button (Step In / Step Out of nested segments); not on the default keyboard.

play_pause.note: p.400 table: 'Left quote or tilde key (above Tab key), Tab key, 5 key, Space bar - Start and stop playback'.

play_in_to_out.note: Keyboard Settings illustration ("Keyboard - MC English (United States)", Editing Guide p.1205); key names from Avid's labelled Windows NT keyboard chart, whose icons match the 2026 illustration key for key

go_to_start.note: p.400: 'Home key - move to the beginning of a clip or sequence'.

go_to_end.note: p.400: 'End key - move to the end of a clip or sequence'.

prev_edit_point.note: Keyboard Settings illustration ("Keyboard - MC English (United States)", Editing Guide p.1205); key names from Avid's labelled Windows NT keyboard chart, whose icons match the 2026 illustration key for key; trim table 'A Previous transition'.

next_edit_point.note: Keyboard Settings illustration ("Keyboard - MC English (United States)", Editing Guide p.1205); key names from Avid's labelled Windows NT keyboard chart, whose icons match the 2026 illustration key for key; trim table 'S Next transition'.

toggle_keyframe.note: Keyboard Settings illustration ("Keyboard - MC English (United States)", Editing Guide p.1205); key names from Avid's labelled Windows NT keyboard chart, whose icons match the 2026 illustration key for key. Avid's only adds a keyframe (does not remove).

zoom_in.note: 2026 guide: 'zooming in or out ... by using Ctrl + [ and Ctrl + ] (Windows)'; direction from the 1999 chart ('Ctrl+] Shows more detail in Timeline') and 2009 sheet.

zoom_out.note: As zoom_in; 1999 chart: 'Ctrl+[ Shows less detail in Timeline'.

toggle_fullscreen.note: 'To disable full screen playback: Type Shift+Ctrl+F'; enabling is via Composer > Full Screen Playback (the guide names the key only for turning it off).

close_project.note: p.~22: 'To close the current project ... Select File > Close Project. Press Ctrl+Shift+W'.

multicam_angle_1.note: 2026 illustration labels F9 'M1'; the MultiCam chapter says angles are cut 'by using the MultiCam keys' and refers to 'the default MultiCam keys'. Also: numeric-keypad 1 switches angles in split views (numpad not writable in Klipp notation; keypad position mapping differs from angle order).

multicam_angle_2.note: 2026 illustration labels F10 'M2'; the MultiCam chapter says angles are cut 'by using the MultiCam keys' and refers to 'the default MultiCam keys'. Also: numeric-keypad 2 switches angles in split views (numpad not writable in Klipp notation; keypad position mapping differs from angle order).

multicam_angle_3.note: 2026 illustration labels F11 'M3'; the MultiCam chapter says angles are cut 'by using the MultiCam keys' and refers to 'the default MultiCam keys'. Also: numeric-keypad 3 switches angles in split views (numpad not writable in Klipp notation; keypad position mapping differs from angle order).

multicam_angle_4.note: 2026 illustration labels F12 'M4'; the MultiCam chapter says angles are cut 'by using the MultiCam keys' and refers to 'the default MultiCam keys'. Also: numeric-keypad 4 switches angles in split views (numpad not writable in Klipp notation; keypad position mapping differs from angle order).

multicam_angle_5.note: Only the numeric keypad: 'Press a number key on the numeric keypad to switch to a new camera angle' (keypad 5 = a split position, e.g. 5 = center, 7 = upper left). Numpad keys cannot be written in Klipp notation; no main-keyboard default.

multicam_angle_6.note: Only the numeric keypad: 'Press a number key on the numeric keypad to switch to a new camera angle' (keypad 6 = a split position, e.g. 5 = center, 7 = upper left). Numpad keys cannot be written in Klipp notation; no main-keyboard default.

multicam_angle_7.note: Only the numeric keypad: 'Press a number key on the numeric keypad to switch to a new camera angle' (keypad 7 = a split position, e.g. 5 = center, 7 = upper left). Numpad keys cannot be written in Klipp notation; no main-keyboard default.

multicam_angle_8.note: Only the numeric keypad: 'Press a number key on the numeric keypad to switch to a new camera angle' (keypad 8 = a split position, e.g. 5 = center, 7 = upper left). Numpad keys cannot be written in Klipp notation; no main-keyboard default.

multicam_angle_9.note: Only the numeric keypad: 'Press a number key on the numeric keypad to switch to a new camera angle' (keypad 9 = a split position, e.g. 5 = center, 7 = upper left). Numpad keys cannot be written in Klipp notation; no main-keyboard default.

not_checked.save_project: Avid saves projects/bins automatically; no Save shortcut is stated in the 2026 guides (File > Save Bin's key not given). The full modifier list lives only in the in-app Help > Shortcuts.
not_checked.import_media: Import (File > Input > Import Media) exists; no default key in the fetched documents (Ctrl+I is Clip Info).
not_checked.export: Export (File > Output > Export) exists; no default key in the fetched documents.
not_checked.new_project: New project is made in the Select Project dialog; no shortcut documented.
not_checked.open_project: Opening a project is via the Select Project dialog after Close Project; no shortcut documented.
not_checked.quit: File > Exit exists; no shortcut documented in the fetched sources.
not_checked.preferences: Avid's Settings (File > Settings) are the nearest; the only key seen is Ctrl+= 'settings for the active window' in the 2009 sheet - not the same thing.
not_checked.create_title: Titler+ / Title Tool exist (Tools / Clip menu); no default key in the fetched documents.
not_checked.toggle_multicam_mode: MultiCamera Mode (Composer menu). The 2026.8 ReadMe names Ctrl+Shift+M as a modifier shortcut 'for Multicam editing' but does not say which command it runs; not recorded as a key.
not_checked.toggle_audio_mixer: Audio Mixer (Tools > Audio Mixer); no key in 2026 docs. Ctrl+1 in the old sheets opens the Audio tool (meters), not the mixer.
not_checked.toggle_color_panel: Color Correction mode/workspace exists; no default key found.
not_checked.toggle_scopes: Scopes exist in Color Correction mode; no default key found.
not_checked.toggle_safe_areas: Safe Title/Action guides via the Grid button in Effect mode; no default key found.
not_checked.toggle_grid_overlay: Effect Grid via the Grid button in Effect mode; no default key found.
not_checked.prev_keyframe: Keyframe navigation commands exist in Effect Editor; no default key found in the fetched docs.

editor_only.command: Toggle Source/Record (switch active monitor); exits Trim mode
Previous In Group / Next In Group (MultiCamera)
Place Markers window info in Console
Select all tracks / Deselect all tracks
New sequence from the active Sequence Template
Capture-mode function keys: subclip IN/OUT, log/capture, colored markers
New video track / New audio track
Select clips/segments copy: Copy to Source monitor / Lift to Source / Extract to Source

add_audio_crossfade.why: \\ is one Media Composer command, Add Dissolve, on the selected tracks; Klipp has two actions, and \\ goes to add_default_transition

trim_tool.why: U is one Media Composer command, Trim Mode, entered at the nearest transition; select_edit_point does that in Klipp, and trim_tool would arm a tool as well
